root.name: Scotch Game: Haxo Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Bc4 Bc5

overview: White leaves the d4 pawn with Black and develops with 5.c3 or 5.O-O, intending a lead in development and e5 or a break against the Black centre. After 5.c3 the pawn on d4 can be kept, so White needs tactics; lines such as 5.c3 Nf6 6.e5 d5 7.Bb5 Ne4 8.cxd4 recover it with open play. The game is open and tactical for both sides.

white_ideas.idea: Play c3 or O-O to open lines, then e5 against ...Nf6 and regain the pawn with cxd4 or Nxd4
Use the c4 bishop and quick development against f7

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn with ...d6 and ...Nf6, solid development
Return it at the right moment with ...d5 for an equal open game

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with Black pawn on d4 or returned to d5; fast development, open e-file

character.notes: Open, concrete play with early tactics around e5 and d5; known for double-edged play.

gambit.notes: After 5.c3 or 5.O-O Black can keep the d-pawn; White needs ...dxc3 or d3 tactics.

soundness.notes: Sound; Black has safe equalising ways and the Scotch Gambit is well regarded.

structure.notes: The centre opens quickly with e-file and diagonals active, as in other Scotch lines.

approach.notes: Played by strong players at times; respectable.

level.notes: Needs knowing the lines (c3, e5 d5 Bb5 Ne4) for White; Black's tries are less forcing.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5.O-O
sublines_that_differ.how: Slower; White gets a Max Lange-type development lead without immediate tactics.

character.reason: A pawn is offered for open lines and quick tactics.

gambit.reason: Black can keep the d4 pawn and White has to regain it by force.

soundness.reason: Accepted as equal with correct play.

structure.reason: Pawns come off in the centre early and the pieces use open lines.

approach.reason: A regular part of the Scotch repertoire.

level.reason: Some theory is needed but not an advanced tree.

plans.reason: White develops quickly with the bishop on c4.
